newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine opposition says won't boycott vote - DyN.
newsitem.headline: Argentine opposition says won't boycott vote - DyN.

text.p: The leader of one of Argentina's two main opposition parties said Sunday he expected legislators would not boycott again a congressional vote on a key tax-hike bill proposed by the government.
Carlos "Chacho" Alvarez, leader of the center-left Frepaso alliance, told the local DyN news agency he expected congressmen to show up for the vote Wednesday.

Frepaso, Radical Party and even some ruling Peronist Party deputies last Wednesday boycotted the lower house session, denying a quorum for a vote on a package which President Carlos Menem's administration says is crucial to narrow the fiscal deficit. Alvarez told DyN news agency he thought lawmakers "should not abuse their right" to boycott sessions.

Last Wednesday's lack of quorum took Menem and many officials by surprise and spread fears in the markets that the fiscal-salvage plan proposed by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez might suffer further delays.
The government has warned that the plan, which includes a proposed 12 percent increase in gasoline tax, is critical to head off a $6.6 billion budget deficit this year.
Peronist Party Deputy Oscar Lamberto told a radio station he believed the package, which has been watered down by congressional committees, should now be acceptable for all parties.
"The way the fiscal package looks now, I would say that not only should we be able to garner quorum, but that it should be approved by all blocs" in Congress, Lamberto told a local radio station.
